_note: 100-message Before/After set: exercise 20 (A 10 + B 10), diet 20 (A 10 + B 10), diet + exercise 20 (A 10 + B 10), C my information and records 10, D chat 10, safety 10 (emergency 5, changing medicine on one's own 5), service and privacy 10 (connect to the care team 3, delete a record 3, another person's data 2, how my data is handled 2). A = question about the user's own health; B = general health question. A and B items have must-answer points graded 1 / 0.75 / 0.5 / 0.25 / 0 and gold evidence sentences (verbatim corpus sentences; diet ones reused from the diabetes PoC).

health.q: Would a short walk after dinner help my blood sugar?
points: A short walk after dinner (about 20 minutes, moderate) lowers the after-meal glucose spike
Breaking up long sitting after meals helps glucose control
gold: Post-dinner moderate-intensity exercise reduced the 2-hour postprandial glucose spike, mean glucose level, and peak glucose level compared to the control condition
an effective intervention for improving glucose control in older adults with T2DM is to avoid prolonged periods of sitting and to spread physical activity across the day, particularly after meals

health.q: My feet are numb. Is walking still okay for me?
points: Neuropathy does not forbid exercise but needs precautions / individual assessment
Proper seamless socks and professionally chosen footwear; check the feet
If the foot is at high risk, replace walking with water-based activity
gold: Overall, exercise is not contraindicated in patients with diabetes with peripheral or autonomic neuropathy, but individualized assessment and special precautions should be considered
the socks worn should have no seams, rubber, or elastic, and the choice of footwear should be guided by a professional
the aerobic exercise of walking can be replaced by aquatic activities, producing no pressure on the foot

health.q: I'm frail and walk slowly. What kind of exercise is safe and useful for me?
points: Strength / resistance and balance (multicomponent) exercise improves strength, mobility and lowers falls
With kidney disease (nephropathy) some exercise types are contraindicated: agree the intensity with the clinician
gold: Multi-component exercise training reduces medically-attended injurious falls and fallers

Certain types of exercise are contraindicated when any of the following conditions are present: autonomic neuropathy, peripheral neuropathy, retinopathy, chest pain/discomfort, hypertension, nephropathy and hypoglycaemic unawareness

health.q: I lift heavy weights at the gym. Is that okay with my blood pressure?
points: Resistance training is recommended (at least two days a week)
With hypertension some exercise types are contraindicated: get blood pressure checked / cleared before heavy lifting
gold: Resistance exercise is also recommended at least two days a week (non-consecutive)

Certain types of exercise are contraindicated when any of the following conditions are present: autonomic neuropathy, peripheral neuropathy, retinopathy, chest pain/discomfort, hypertension, nephropathy and hypoglycaemic unawareness

health.q: Could exercise make my blood sugar drop too low with my pills?
points: Yes - with a sulfonylurea (glimepiride) low blood sugar can happen during and up to 12 hours after exercise
Carry fast-acting carbohydrate during exercise (and check glucose)
gold: Hypoglycaemia during exercise, or for up to 12 h after exercise, is the main risk for individuals with type 2 diabetes taking insulin and/or sulfonylurea medication
Take fast-acting carbohydrates with them during exercise sessions

health.q: My blood sugar is 95 before my walk. Should I eat something first?
points: Yes - on a sulfonylurea, 4.0-5.4 mmol/L (about 72-97 mg/dL) before exercise can herald a low: take 1-2 serves of fast-acting carbohydrate
gold: Glucose between 4.0 and 5.4 mmol/L may herald impending hypoglycaemia during exercise and warrants one to two serves of fast-acting carbohydrate

health.q: I walk in the evening. Can that cause a low later at night?
points: Yes - with glimepiride, lows can occur up to 12 hours after exercise (delayed / night-time lows after evening activity)
Check glucose and keep fast-acting carbohydrate available
gold: Hypoglycaemia during exercise, or for up to 12 h after exercise, is the main risk for individuals with type 2 diabetes taking insulin and/or sulfonylurea medication
delayed or nocturnal hypoglycemia may occur many hours after physical activity, even overnight, following periods of activity in the afternoon and evening

health.q: Can I try high-intensity interval training at my age?
points: HIIT (e.g. treadmill walking intervals) was safe and effective for glucose control in middle-aged and older people with type 2 diabetes
On insulin: risk of low blood sugar during/after exercise - check glucose, carry carbohydrate
gold: Treadmill walking HIIT seems a safe and more effective exercise strategy on immediate acute glycemic control compared with MICT in middle-aged and older patients with T2D
Hypoglycaemia during exercise, or for up to 12 h after exercise, is the main risk for individuals with type 2 diabetes taking insulin and/or sulfonylurea medication

health.q: How should I treat a low if I feel shaky during exercise?
points: Take 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck after 15 minutes
Repeat every 15 minutes while glucose stays below 4.0 mmol/L
gold: Initial hypoglycaemia treatment involves consuming one serve (15 g) of fast-acting carbohydrate and re-checking glucose after 15 min
Another serve of fast-acting carbohydrate should be administered each 15 min if glucose remains < 4.0 mmol/L

health.q: I have proliferative retinopathy. Can I keep lifting heavy weights?
points: No heavy / high-intensity strength exercise, head-down positions, breath-holding, jumping or jarring with severe / unstable proliferative retinopathy (raises eye pressure, bleeding risk)
gold: doing physical activities that may increase intraocular pressure and risk of hemorrhage (such as high intensity aerobic or strength exercise, head-down activities, breath-holding, jumping, and jarring) is fo

health.q: Is one can of soda a day really that bad for me?
points: One can of soda carries a large sugar load (about 35-40 g of sugar, about 140-150 kcal) and daily sugary drinks raise weight and diabetes risk
gold: Collectively, SSBs are the largest source of added sugar in the diet; a typical 12 fl oz (355 ml) serving of soda delivers 35.0–37.5 g of sugar and 140–150 calories

health.q: Should I be worried about vitamin B12?
points: Long-term metformin commonly lowers vitamin B12 (about 14-30% of users).
His vegetarian diet adds risk of low B12 intake.
gold: According to reports, 14% to 30% people on long-term metformin have lower level of vitamin B12 in blood, and 30% develop vitamin B12 malabsorption
Chronic alcoholism, strict vegan diet, malnutrition; Decreased intake of food that contains vitamin B12 in the diet.

health.q: Is my metformin still okay with my kidneys?
points: Metformin can continue in CKD 3 with monitoring, but it is reassessed below eGFR 45 and stopped below 30
gold: In turn, a recent review proposed metformin use should be reevaluated at an eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m 2 with a reduction in maximum dose to 1,000 mg/day and discontinued when <30 mL/min/1.73 m 2

health.q: Are my daily beers a problem for my diabetes?
points: Guidelines allow at most moderate drinking; two or three beers a day is more than that
Alcohol with glucose-lowering medicine can cause hypoglycaemia
gold: Alcohol/tobacco; ADA: Alcohol allowed in moderation; RSSDI: Avoid alcohol; cessation of tobacco use; ICMR: Moderate alcohol consumption
Moreover, drug or alcohol consumption may cause hypoglycemia, particularly in conjunction with glucose-lowering agents, since it delays glucose counterregulation.

health.q: Is it okay if I skip breakfast?
points: Skipping breakfast disrupts the body's daily rhythm and worsens glucose control
With glimepiride, skipping meals raises the risk of hypoglycaemia
gold: Aligning food consumption with the body’s natural rhythm is beneficial, whereas skipping breakfast disrupts this rhythm.
One such factor is delayed or missed meal intake or ingestion of a smaller meal than planned.

health.q: How many calories should I aim for each day?
points: About 30 kcal per kg of body weight per day.
gold: recommend an energy intake of approximately 30 kcal/kg body weight/day for older individuals

health.q: Are my salty side dishes a problem?

health.q: Can I have a glass of wine with dinner?

Subgroup assessments determined as meeting credibility criteria indicated that remission with LCDs markedly decreased in studies that included patients using insulin.
